title: Freelance Business Checklist

lessons.title: Course Material: Freelance-Business-Checklist.pdf
lessons.content:
PAGE_1:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 1  Start Your Own Freelance Business – Checklist  Introduction ü Becoming a freelancer is one of the easiest and fastest ways to start your own business ü Freelancers offer unique skills and talents to individuals or companies in return for a fee ü Small business owners normally try to outsource production as soon as possible ü Freelance business owners continue to produce the bulk of the product themselves  The Freelance Life: Pros and Cons  Pros ü Freelancers choose who they work with ü No office politics ü Flexibility ü Variety ü Freedom Cons ü Taxes ü No Benefits ü ‘Feast or Famine’ ü Self-Promotion

PAGE_2:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 2  ü Ultimate Responsibility  Why Start a Freelance Business? ü Being a freelancer gives you freedom to design a lifestyle you love ü Freelancing also gives you the option to keep your day job  Here is your roadmap through the course: 
   Learning Objectives:  By the time you complete this course, you’ll be able to:  ü Identify your marketable skills, niche, and target audience ü Manage your freelance finances ü Set up the administrative and operational aspects of your business  Choose Your Niche and Target AudienceGet a Handle on Your FinancesSet Up Operations and AdministrationDevelop Your Freelance BrandMarket Your Freelance BusinessFind and Convert ClientsMaintain Client Relationships

PAGE_3:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 3  ü Define and articulate a personal brand that attracts your target audience ü Develop your website, portfolio, and social media presence  ü Find and convert clients through the right channels  ü Cultivate client relationships while also setting boundaries and staying top of mind ü Review your financial targets, client relationships, and client feedback, and then apply    Expectations Before we start the course, take a minute to think about what you want to get out of it. In the Action Guide, write down three skills you expect to gain.

PAGE_4:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 4  Module 1 – Identify Your Niche and Target Audience   Learning Objective: ü Identify your marketable skills, niche, and target audience that will enable you to build a successful and sustainable freelance business  Lesson 1: Choose a Freelance Niche  Key Takeaways: ü Your niche is a combination of the service you are uniquely qualified to provide and a problem you can solve for a specific group of people. ü Establish a niche to differentiate yourself from other service providers.  ü Define your niche by reviewing your CV, interests and passions, work and life experience, expertise, and education.  ü You need to identify the talents and marketable skills you possess that people are willing to pay for ü This may be as simple as using current career skills ü Here are some careers with ‘freelance potential’: o Graphic designer  o Writer/copywriter  o Social media content creator o Accountant  o Bookkeeper

PAGE_5:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 5  o Developer o Translator  o Videographer  o Virtual assistant  o SEO consultant  o Podcast producer  ü Once you’ve chosen a general service, you need to narrow it down to a niche ü Your niche is a combination of the service you are uniquely qualified to provide and a problem you can solve for a specific group of people  Define Your Niche ü Define your niche by first looking at your CV and seeing what stands out ü Also consider what you are passionate about ü Think about areas of expertise outside your current career ü Keep your portfolio in mind

PAGE_6:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 6  Action Steps: 1. If you haven’t decided on the service you will offer, brainstorm 5 ideas now. Think about the marketable skills and talents you have been recognized for and list them in your Action Guide.  2. Write down the service you plan on providing. 3. Once you know what service you will provide, it is time to narrow it down further and establish your niche. To help you with this, answer the following questions in your Action Guide: a. What stands out on your CV? List the specific skills you excel at and have been recognized for.  b. Narrow these down even further: What do you enjoy so much that it almost doesn’t feel like work?  c. What are you passionate about? What do you enjoy doing, researching, or learning about even if you don’t get paid to do it?  d. Do you have specialized knowledge or skills that friends, neighbors, social media followers, or associates reach out to you for help with?  e. Is there a skill or subject matter that you went to school for that may translate into a freelance career? f. Is there a personal experience, struggle you’ve overcome, or passion that you could turn into a freelance career? 4. Reflect on your answers to number 3, decide on your niche and write it down.

PAGE_7:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 7  Lesson 2: Define Your Target Audience   Key Takeaways: Ø To define your audience, create a profile of the person who needs your specific skills and service.  Ø Make sure your target audience is a profitable segment.  Ø Your target audience may be other businesses. But there is always an individual within these organizations that you will need to pitch.   ü Think about who needs your skills and services ü Be specific ü Once you have a general profile, analyze the following: o Demographics o Psychographics ü You’ll need have a profitable segment ü Make sure your target audience is: o Large enough to sustain your business  o Familiar to you o Underserved o Easy to find.  o Ready for your solution  o Able to pay for your service

PAGE_8:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 8  Business-to-Business ü Your target audience may also be other businesses ü There is always an individual within each of these organizations that you will need to pitch to    Action Steps:  1. Identify the target audience for your freelance niche by answering the following questions in your Action Guide: a. Who is the audience that would most benefit from your services?  b. What solutions can you provide this audience? c. Identify them based on demographics: age, marital status, profession, geographic location etc.  2. Make sure the target audience you identified will be able to sustain your freelance business by answering the following questions in your Action Guide: a. Are there enough of these people to sustain your business? b. Are they easy to find? c. Are they ready for your solution? d. Can they afford your solution?

PAGE_9:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 9  Module 2 - Get a Handle on Your Finances  Learning Objective: ü Manage your freelance finances so you can establish a profitable freelance rate and set targets to measure your success  Lesson 1: Estimate Expenses and Establish Your Rate  Key Takeaway: ü Understand your expenses before you determine your rate. ü It is essential that you set an hourly rate, even if it is only for your own reference. ü Add 10% to your estimated total monthly expenses to allow for unexpected expenses   ü Take a look at all the items you need to establish and operate your business ü You’ll need to separate out your expenses and have a good idea of costs  Expense Categories ü Some of the expense categories you will need to consider: o Software/Applications and service subscriptions

PAGE_10:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 10  o Office or meeting space (rental, coworking costs etc.) o Utilities (electricity, internet connection, mobile data etc.) o Website (domain registration, site hosting, web design) o Travel (gas/mileage, transportation, parking) o Advertising and marketing  o Accounting fees o Education  Establish Your Rate ü Once you understand your costs, you can establish an hourly rate ü Your expectations need to be realistic  Do the Math  ü Estimate the number of billable hours in a year ü Don’t forget to subtract holidays and vacation time ü Plug the above numbers into the following formula:  o [Yearly expenses] ÷ [Billable hours in a year] = Minimum Hourly rate ü This formula is oversimplified, but serves as a general idea ü It’ll keep you realistic and focused on your goals ü There are online resources that allow you to compare average freelance rates ü Use them to help generate a ballpark figure

PAGE_11:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 11    Action Steps:  1. Using the Finances Spreadsheet, record your start-up costs and monthly expenses.  a. Estimate monthly expenses based on what you know now (these expenses may change as you learn more about how your business operates).  b. Record your billable hours per week and estimated vacation/ holiday time. This will calculate the minimum hourly rate necessary to cover your monthly expenses. 2. Your hourly rate also needs to take into account the value that you bring to the table. In your Action Guide, list relevant experience and education related to your freelance business that show the value you bring.  3. Visit websites like Clockify that provide average hourly rates for freelancers in your industry. These sites will often list different rates based on the freelancer’s experience. When selecting your ‘expertise level’, consider past experience gained through your education and work and volunteer experience (so even if you are just starting out as a freelancer, you may not necessarily be a ‘beginner’). 4. Using the information gathered from the above steps, set your hourly rate and record it in the Finances Spreadsheet.

PAGE_12:
IAPWE Professional Development Series 12  Lesson 2: Set Up Your Accounting System   Key Takeaways: ü Consider cloud-based accounting software to track income and expenses, generate invoices, and share numbers with your accountant in real time. ü Enlisting the help of an accountant throughout the year to save you time and money in the long run.   ü Consider cloud-based accounting software like QuickBooks to track income and expenses ü You can also enlist the help of an accountant ü Work with an accountant through
